record.review: narrow SOURCE closure of recoverable media registry publication failure handling

inputs.reviewedRegions: owned transaction and publication recovery, 123-126 and 159-215

inputs.role: reserveDirectory and commit contracts retained from prior review

evidence: A fresh exclusively reserved transaction directory owns the staged registry. Its removal defer is conditional on preserveTransaction.
Before publication, existing receipt bytes are bounded and copied raw into the transaction. The registry swap's returned prior-file location is retained in oldRegistry.

After successful publication, the final-path helper, validation and readiness publication remain inside a do/catch. Any Swift error in that region sets preserveTransaction before attempting recovery metadata, emits a diagnostic naming the transaction, and rethrows the original error.

The failure path neither restores nor deletes the live registry/receipt, so it does not clobber an independently changed destination. The prior registry and receipt bytes survive in the owned directory when present.
Successful completion leaves preserveTransaction false, allowing best-effort cleanup of the prior backup directory. No automatic rollback is claimed.

limits: Recovery metadata writing uses try? and can fail under storage errors; the preserve flag is already set and the diagnostic still names the retained directory. This is recoverable prior-byte retention, not a guarantee that recovery.json can always be written on a failing filesystem.

No live-cache restoration or automatic recovery is performed. A later authorized preparation must validate/regenerate current runtime state; the retained bytes are diagnostic/recovery material, not an adopted ready state.
Success-directory removal is best effort. An unremoved successful transaction is not evidence of a preparation failure.
No helper, fault injection, registry swap, cancellation, build or runtime result was executed or independently audited. Earlier broader reports remain their recorded snapshots.

record.review: bounded SOURCE audit of media preparation product-callsite integration

reviewed: CLI Run/Steam integration and launch callback
GUI early activity/inherited handoff and feedback owner

verdict.basis: The reviewed new launch paths own preparation and spawn with activity checks, place cold preparation before the outer bottle transactions, preserve original caller checks and CLI wait semantics, and leave stop/control launches without automatic cold work. This is source assessment only, not proof of actual cancellation, UI behavior, helper execution, or Wine/media acceptance.

checkedProperties.result: LaunchPreparation verifies the bottle/prefix/engine relationship, then enters InstallationActivity.perform around preparation and work(prepared). Its checked runner appends activity and caller checks to the incoming runner. The internal perform reuses an inherited same-bottle ticket, checks before/after work and orders finish against cancellation; otherwise it creates and finishes a ticket. Preparation remains within that ownership interval rather than occurring in a detached untracked helper operation.

Start's initial read-only existing-instance scan can avoid needless preparation, but the authoritative matching/spawn decision is repeated inside prepared.withBottleOperation after preparation. Restart also calls LaunchPreparation before entering that outer bottle transaction; it then performs the existing stop, checks cancellation and makes the final matching/spawn decision under the lock. No slow service invocation occurs in the final locked closure. Stop itself and Steam -shutdown retain their ordinary no-auto-preparation path.

checkedProperties.area: runner dependency phase and final launch guard
checkedProperties.result: preparingMedia composes Task cancellation with the previous runner check, retains that check in returned copies, validates plan/current configuration/preflight/clone/PatchState, and rejects managed cold preparation under its calling bottle lock. Explicit expert GST overrides retain their skip behavior. A prepared runner only performs read-only requirePrepared under final bottle->engine authority. Bottle/engine lock waits and the final pre-Spawn point use the retained launchCheck. The new integration does not replace existing guards or make launch automatically run the cold helper.

checkedProperties.area: CLI Run --wait callback and no replay
checkedProperties.result: Run still builds its original plan/environment/cwd and uses the original runner.runToCompletion for --wait. The optional launching callback invokes LaunchPreparation once; because its return type is nonoptional, a thrown callback does not fall back to a second launch. With no callback the original launch path remains. After callback launch, the existing session PID wait, observation behavior, original runner post-wait check, Task cancellation handling and bottle idle wait remain present. The inner launch activity can finish at spawn without making a finished-ticket check poison the later wait.

checkedProperties.area: CLI non-wait Run and both Steam entry points
checkedProperties.result: Non-wait Run, Steam game launch and Steam install request now explicitly enter LaunchPreparation with the existing runner and observer check. Progress remains on the GUI-hosted command context. No standalone CLI/bridge Wine-spawning path is introduced by these callsites. Observer detachment during prelaunch work can abort that work; after a program has launched the original wait/observation semantics remain separate from an explicit bottle Stop.

checkedProperties.area: new bottle reservation and first Wine child
checkedProperties.result: BottleStore.create retains its reservation/caller ownership check in the runner, writes configuration, prepares media, and only then marks initializationStarted and invokes the first wineboot. This stage is before an outer bottle-operation transaction. The existing BottlePreparation reservation activity therefore remains the owner when used by product creation, while lower-level callers retain their supplied initialization check. No preparation is added to engine import or runner construction.

ManualInstaller keeps its caller Activity check on the incoming runner and routes the captured collector plan through LaunchPreparation; its Running result still retains the original outer activity for wait/status handling. If a TaskLocal is not inherited there can be an additional coordinator ticket, but both belong to the same stop domain and the original caller check remains composed. RecipeInstaller already owns InstallationActivity.perform; its checked runner explicitly prepares before installer, registry and winver launches, keeping those preparations outside the corresponding prefix-operation calls. Existing collector/status evidence is not replaced with native helper success.

checkedProperties.area: GUI early Activity and cancellation into detached work
checkedProperties.result: Library start/restart registers or accepts its activity before setting busy state and creating the asynchronous task. The worker explicitly executes activity.performing and retains both incoming launchCheck and activity.checkCancellation on its runner. Cancellation handlers cancel that activity, reaching helper polling even though Task.detached does not inherit the parent's cancellation automatically. Tool, custom command and patch-installer paths likewise register before dispatch and use the completing ownership wrapper for prep+spawn. Existing Stop can see registered work rather than only a busy flag.

checkedProperties.area: recipe handoff does not finish borrowed ownership
checkedProperties.result: The new GUI launch(item, using: activity) passes the existing Activity as preparationActivity. The launch action computes ownsActivity=false for that inherited case and uses performing rather than completing. The recipe task retains ownership across refresh/auto-launch, rechecks cancellation/owner UUID afterwards and performs the final activity.finish itself. One-shot GUI launches finish their own activity after the worker's prep/spawn phase; later feedback/process observation does not schedule another Wine launch.

AppLaunchFeedback is MainActor-isolated. New worker progress callbacks hop to MainActor, check the activity where appropriate and update the same generation box through updateFeedback; final messages use that owner. The box is feedback ownership, not the cancellation authority: activity and runner checks remain responsible for Stop/spawn safety. No concrete new cross-actor mutable-generation race was found in the inspected callbacks.

controlAndScopeBoundaries: Existing Kill/bottle Stop remains the shared stoppingInstallations + Windows drain path. The reviewed code does not automatically run media preparation in killAll, wineserver -k/-w, or AppLifecycle.stop. A canceled helper must still be reaped before its owning preparation returns; that is the previously reviewed service/command contract, not runtime evidence supplied here.

Old maintenance/bookkeeping Wine calls are outside this newly wired launch scope and were not reported as missing DMO/product preparation hooks. No request to add automatic cold work to those controls is made.

The ticket domain guarantees cancellation for already-owned work. This audit does not establish a new global admission generation ordering every queued request before or after Stop; UI feedbackGeneration is not such a fence.
The same checked runner must be retained for the actual prepared plan and final spawn. Expert GST overrides are not certified by a default managed-registry preparation receipt.

Some GUI activity ownership ends at successful one-shot spawn while refresh/pending-message bookkeeping follows. This report does not turn that bookkeeping into helper/Wine execution or claim broader UI state-machine acceptance.

No source compilation, tests, helper execution, actual Stop/late-launch interleaving, UI behavior, Wine launch, DMO/codec result, package identity or runtime receipt was executed or independently audited. The parent's vendor-helper positive/negative work remains separate evidence.
evidenceLimits: Only the changed integration callsites, their direct activity/runner contracts and the narrow service backup change were read. No new broad DMO, old control, scheduler, Windows or kernel audit was performed.

No implementation or test files, engines, bottles, defaults or runtime state were edited. Only this report and the separately requested media-service-source-review-v3.json were produced for the two scoped reviews.
